comparisons.peer_topic: Purpose and nature of non-GAAP measures
comparisons.peer_summary: The company presents non-GAAP financial measures as additional useful information to assess financial condition and operating performance, though they are not a substitute for GAAP measures and may differ from peers.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and BAC explicitly define and discuss the use of non-GAAP financial measures in their disclosures. JPM states that 'Net interest income excluding Markets and adjusted expense are non-GAAP financial measures.' Similarly, BAC presents a section dedicated to 'non-GAAP financial measures,' explaining that they exclude certain items to assess financial condition and are not intended as a substitute for GAAP measures.

sentences.text: Net interest income excluding Markets and adjusted expense are non-GAAP financial measures.
In this Form 10-K, we present certain non-GAAP financial measures.
Non-GAAP financial measures exclude certain items or otherwise include components that differ from the most directly comparable measures calculated in accordance with GAAP.

Non-GAAP financial measures are provided as additional useful information to assess our financial condition, results of operations (including period-to-period operating performance) or compliance with prospective regulatory requirements.

comparisons.peer_topic: Net Interest Income Growth and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income for 2024 was $8.06 billion, representing a 27% increase from 2023, driven by higher interest income from trading assets, investments, and collateralized agreements due to higher balances and rates, partially offset by a decrease in deposits with banks.
comparisons.comparison: While JPM provides forward-looking guidance for 2025 net interest income ($94.0 billion), GS discloses historical 2024 results showing significant growth in this metric. JPM expects NII to be market dependent, whereas GS reports a 27% year-over-year increase in NII for 2024 to $8.06 billion, driven by higher interest income from trading assets and investments. Both disclosures focus on the dynamics and drivers of net interest income as a key financial measure.

sentences.text: • Management expects net interest income to be approximately $94.0 billion and net interest income excluding Markets to be approximately $90.0 billion, market dependent.

Net interest income in the consolidated statements of earnings was $8.06 billion for 2024, 27% higher than 2023, reflecting an increase in interest income, partially offset by an increase in interest expense.

The increase in interest income primarily related to trading assets and investments (each reflecting the impact of higher average balances and higher average interest rates), collateralized agreements and other interest-earning assets (each reflecting the impact of higher average interest rates), partially offset by a decrease in interest income related to deposits with banks (reflecting the impact of lower average balances).

peer_results.rationale: Candidates focus on the attribution of average common equity to business segments as a non-GAAP measure and the composition of net interest income within Wealth Management. These are specific segment-level accounting definitions and risk composition details. JPM's disclosure is a consolidated full-year forward guidance statement for net interest income and expenses. The MS disclosures do not provide comparable forward-looking guidance or consolidated non-GAAP reconciliations for the same metrics.
